authority: T0 exact analytic classical semidiscrete candidate certificate; not a TECT claim, tier change, Goursat discretization, regulator-removal theorem, CP1 completion, or Pre-A closure
statement: For a separately supplied sufficiently smooth solution of the declared eight-species CL8 Cauchy problem on a fixed periodic one-dimensional physical domain and fixed finite time, the centered spatial semidiscretization with the inherited a/8 per-unit-transverse-area ledger converges at O(a^2) in the weighted discrete H1_a times L2_a phase norm. Each finite regulator exactly conserves its Hamiltonian and variational symplectic form. An Arb-enclosed one-mode linearized regression independently exhibits the expected factor-four refinement ratio. The theorem is not a semidiscrete Goursat scheme and does not compose characteristic data with lattice initial data.
verdict: ADVANCE FIXED-DOMAIN SMOOTH-CAUCHY O(a^2) CONVERGENCE; RETAIN NONZERO FINITE-a TAILS AND KEEP THE BOUNDARY-TO-LATTICE COMPOSITION OPEN

definition.domain: T_L=R/(LZ), with a=L/M and periodic nodes x_j=ja; the inherited CP1 subsequence takes even M so the fine N=2M regulator remains divisible by four
definition.potential: the same eight-species Q3 polynomial W as PA-CP1-CL8-GOURSAT-v0
definition.parameter_domain: chi>0, c>0, g>0, lambda>=0, r real

hamiltonian_structure.equations: psi_dot=Pi/chi and Pi_dot=c Delta_a psi-grad W(psi)
hamiltonian_structure.exact_invariants: dH_a/dt=0 and d Omega_a((xi,varpi),(eta,vartheta))/dt=0 for any two variational solutions
hamiltonian_structure.global_finite_regulator_existence: the positive onsite quartic and nonnegative Q3 lock make the finite potential coercive up to its exact additive lower bound; conserved energy prevents finite-time escape

analytic_theorem.initial_error: the modified error energy E_alpha(0)^(1/2)<=C_init*a^2 for fixed alpha>0; exact sampled Cauchy data give C_init=0
analytic_theorem.residual: tau_a=Delta_a R_a psi-R_a psi_xx and ||tau_a||_a<=a^2 sqrt(L/8)[M4/12+a^2 M6/360]
analytic_theorem.uniform_rate: for every fixed L,T and a<=a_* there is an a-independent C_T with sup_{0<=t<=T} E_alpha(t)^(1/2)<=C_T*a^2
analytic_theorem.bootstrap: the uniform discrete one-dimensional Sobolev bound closes the radius-R interval for sufficiently small a
analytic_theorem.rate_scope: weighted discrete H1_a times L2_a only; piecewise-linear reconstruction is not claimed to converge at O(a^2) in continuous H1

consistency_coefficients.manufactured_residual: for psi_e=alpha_e(1+t)x^4 the discrete-minus-continuum residual is -2c alpha_e(1+t)a^2; the pointwise nonlinear force cancels from the comparison

tail_corollary.statement: if the separately supplied smooth continuum Cauchy solution vanishes on a declared grid subset K_a(t), then ||psi^a||_{L2_a(K_a)}<=||psi^a-R_a psi||_a<=C a^2 on the fixed interval
tail_corollary.cone_instance: smooth compactly supported continuum data give such subsets strictly outside the inserted continuum cone before periodic wraparound
tail_corollary.scope: aggregate weighted L2 disappearance only; no pointwise, exponential, operator-norm, exact-support, moving-boundary, or boundary-Goursat tail theorem
tail_corollary.finite_a_boundary: the registered strict-cone packages retain particular nonzero variational witness channels at every fixed a; this O(a^2) theorem neither proves nor requires a nonzero tail for every matched smooth datum

arb_regression.scope: one Fourier mode of the zero-background linearization; g and lambda may be positive because their quartic Hessians vanish at zero
arb_regression.certified_checks: 160-bit Arb intervals are positive and decreasing, every successive ratio is in (3.97,4.01), and the M=256 normalized error lies within 1e-5 of sin(sqrt(2)/2)/(48sqrt(2))
arb_regression.analytic_authority: the modified-energy theorem, not the regression, proves the nonlinear O(a^2) rate

composition_gate.separation: this theorem receives a smooth continuum Cauchy solution and lattice Cauchy data separately; it does not receive A,B characteristic traces from the Goursat package
missing: a proved Goursat-slice-to-grid initialization and compatible periodic domain
uniform regularity of the composed slice map in the theorem norms
energy and symplectic consistency under sampling and reconstruction
classical-measure convergence and a common selected quantum state
a treatment of moving characteristic boundaries or ghost values

inserted_inputs: the fixed periodic domain L and time horizon T
the smooth continuum Cauchy solution and its C6 spatial bounds
the centered periodic semidiscretization and sampled or O(a^2)-matched initial data
the one-eighth physical grid normalization and the Q3 potential
derived_outputs: the exact consistency and remainder coefficients
the modified-energy O(a^2) discrete phase-norm estimate
bootstrap closure for sufficiently small a
finite-regulator Hamiltonian and variational symplectic conservation

prior_art_boundary: Second-order central-difference consistency, modified-energy convergence for semilinear wave equations, periodic summation by parts, finite Hamiltonian symplectic flows, and rigorous interval regression are established techniques. No world-first or new general theorem is claimed. The repository-specific result is the exact CL8/Q3 potential and one-eighth normalization audit, the explicit nonlinear constants, and the separation of smooth Cauchy convergence from the still-open characteristic boundary composition.
no_overclaim: This package proves a fixed-domain, fixed-time smooth classical Cauchy semidiscretization theorem in a weighted discrete norm. It does not prove an exact finite-a cone, a semidiscrete Goursat problem, pointwise or exponential tails, convergence for nonsmooth or arbitrary lattice-frequency data, continuous piecewise-linear H1 O(a^2), growing-time or thermodynamic uniformity, full 3+1 or quantum regulator removal, a boundary-to-lattice state map, physical empty space, a below-empty-space sign, cooling, gravity, CP1, or Pre-A.
